name: ResMed Inc.
moat_justification: Dominant global CPAP franchise (~48% global share; US share estimated far higher while Philips Respironics has been out of the US market since its 2021 recall) with a large installed base that throws off recurring mask/resupply revenue, a cloud ecosystem (AirView/myAir) embedded in provider workflows, a deep patent portfolio, and proven pricing/margin power (FY2026 gross margin expanded 290bp, non-GAAP EPS +17% on +10% revenue). Capped at 7, not higher: Philips is expected to re-enter the US (analysts point to FY2028), Fisher & Paykel and low-cost BMC compete on masks/devices, GLP-1 therapy is a long-run narrative headwind even though current claims data shows it aiding PAP starts/adherence, and the core is concentrated in one therapy category — plus a live Astral ventilator Class I recall/sales suspension.
fragility_flags: OE_VOLATILE: OE/share range over the last 5 yrs spans >3x — normalized base helps but the business is cyclical; widen bear weight
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 5.2x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
one_liner: High-quality dominant CPAP franchise, moat 7/10, net cash — but at $234.25 it does not clear 15% (weighted IRR 10.7%, IV@15% $144.57); it clears 15% only at or below ~$145.
moat_for: Dominant CPAP share (~48% global; US share est. much higher with Philips out since 2021 recall)
Installed base drives recurring masks/resupply revenue
AirView/myAir cloud ecosystem embedded in provider and patient workflows
Deep patent portfolio and regulatory/reimbursement know-how
Proven pricing and margin power — FY26 gross margin +290bp, EPS growing faster than revenue
moat_against: Philips Respironics US re-entry expected (analysts point to FY2028) caps share gains
Fisher & Paykel and low-cost BMC/React compete in masks and devices
GLP-1 drugs are a long-run OSA-treatment narrative headwind
Astral ventilator Class I recall — FY27 sales suspended, $42M Q4 charge
